is_anopheles.evidence: The study investigates Anopheles gambiae complex mosquitoes including An. gambiae s.s., An. arabiensis, and a newly identified Pwani molecular form (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Reports target-site mutations Vgsc L995S (L1014S) and Rdl A296S in Figure 5, Cyp6p4 I236M on page 9, and Cyp6aa1 CNV (Dup1) on pages 9-10 and Figure 6A. Also screened Ace-1 G280S (reported as G289S/G119S, 0% observed across cohorts, Figure 5).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides sample numbers per species and location (e.g., Moshi An. arabiensis N=40; Tarime An. arabiensis N=47; Muleba An. arabiensis N=137; Muleba An. gambiae N=32; Muheza An. gambiae N=32; Muheza Pwani form N=10), and Figure 5 gives exact allele frequencies across cohorts (e.g., Vgsc L995S: 98% in Muleba An. gambiae, 41% in Muheza An. gambiae; Rdl A296S: 15% in Moshi An. arabiensis).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were field-collected in Tanzania across four locations: Zeneti village in Muheza, Mabogini in Moshi, Komaswa village in Tarime, and Muleba district (page 3, section 2.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary population genomic research article analyzing whole-genome sequence data of wild Tanzanian Anopheles gambiae complex mosquitoes to characterize population structure, cryptic taxa, and insecticide resistance markers.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific sub-country sites and coordinates are reported: Zeneti village in Muheza (-5.217 S, 38.650 E), lower Mabogini in Moshi (-3.400 S, 37.350 E), Komaswa village in Tarime (-1.417 S, 34.183 E), and Muleba district (1.750 S, 31.667 E) (page 3, section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Specific collection windows are reported per site: Moshi (August-September 2012), Tarime (August 2012), Muheza (November 2012 to May 2013), and Muleba (2015) (page 3, section 2.1; Table 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The authors explicitly note that 'This study used data from the An. gambiae 1000 Genomes Project (Ag1000G) Phase 3 (3.0 release), comprising mosquitoes from Tanzania that were collected in four regions, Muheza and Moshi in north east, and Muleba and Tarime in the north-western regions' (page 3, section 2.1).

supplement.evidence: Key genotype frequencies and sample sizes per cohort are presented directly within the main text (Table 1, Figure 5, Figure 6A, and Results section 3.3).

assessment.summary: This study analyzed whole-genome sequencing data of 300 Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes from four regions in northern Tanzania (Moshi, Tarime, Muheza, and Muleba) generated as part of Ag1000G Phase 3. It identified a new cryptic coastal taxon ('Pwani molecular form') and reported frequencies for key resistance markers including Vgsc L995S, Rdl A296S, Cyp6p4 I236M, and Cyp6aa1 Dup1 across cohorts.
